Voltage is not the same as energy. Voltage is the energy per unit charge. Thus, a motorcycle battery and a car battery can both have the same voltage (more precisely, the same potential difference between battery terminals), yet one stores much more energy than the other because ΔU=qΔV.ΔU=qΔV. The car battery can move more charge than the motorcycle battery, although both are 12-V batteries.
